plan: [ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value. My value is 9, so I bid 9. This ensures I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below 9 and I pay that second-highest bid, guaranteeing nonnegative surplus. Bidding above 9 risks paying more than my value; bidding below 9 risks losing profitable auctions. No prior rounds to learn from in this single-round game. ]

[ Second-price auctions make truthful bidding optimal. With independent private values drawn uniformly each round and only 1 round, there’s no benefit to strategic shading or signaling. Bidding my value ensures I win exactly when the second-highest bid is below my value and I never pay above it. Tie-breaking is random; bidding exactly my value remains optimal. Therefore, to maximize expected profit this round, I will bid my true value of $40. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction (Vickrey). The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true private value because my bid only affects the win/lose decision; payment equals the second-highest bid. No beneficial shading exists, even with risk of ties resolved randomly. With value $32 and $0.1 increments, bid exactly 32.0 to maximize expected profit. ]
